results.title: Search in a singly-linked list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a node pool with $n$ cells, a head $h$ that is either an identity in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ or NIL, and a target payload $t$, the search for $t$ from $h$ is fuel-bounded search for $t$ from $h$ with fuel $n$. It follows next pointers from $h$ and returns the first visited identity whose node has payload $t$, returning nothing if it reaches NIL or an unallocated cell first, or if $n$ steps run out.

results.title: Fuel-bounded search finds the first matching represented identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Suppose a node pool represents, from the head $h$, the list of distinct identities $\ell$. Then for every target payload $t$ and every fuel $f$ with $f \ge |\ell|$, fuel-bounded search for $t$ from $h$ with fuel $f$ returns the first identity in $\ell$ whose cell holds a node with payload $t$, and returns nothing if no identity in $\ell$ has this property.

results.title: Represented lists fit in the store
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix a capacity $n$, let $s$ be a store assigning to each identity below $n$ either nothing or a singly linked list node, and let $\mathrm{head}$ be an identity below $n$ or NIL. If $s$ and $\mathrm{head}$ represent the list of identities $i_0, \dots, i_{k-1}$, then $k \le n$.

results.title: Search finds the first matching represented identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a node pool represents, from the head $h$, the list of distinct identities $\ell$, then for every target payload $t$ the search for $t$ from $h$ returns the first identity in $\ell$ whose cell holds a node with payload $t$, and returns nothing if no identity in $\ell$ has this property.

results.title: A successful search returns a matching represented identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a node pool represents, from the head $h$, the list of distinct identities $\ell$, and the search for a target payload $t$ from $h$ returns an identity $x$, then $x$ belongs to $\ell$ and cell $x$ holds a node with payload $t$.

results.title: Search fails exactly when no represented node has the target payload
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a node pool represents, from the head $h$, the list of distinct identities $\ell$, then for every target payload $t$ the search for $t$ from $h$ returns nothing if and only if no identity in $\ell$ has a cell holding a node with payload $t$.

results.title: Height of a line at an abscissa

results.title: A non-vertical segment is the graph of its line
results.caption: Theorem

A point $z$ lies on the segment from $p$ to $q$ if and only if $p_1 \le z_1 \le q_1$ and $z_2$ is the height at abscissa $z_1$ of the line through $p$ and $q$.

results.title: DIRECTION as a scaled vertical offset

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ map a type to a linearly ordered set, let $y$ be a value, and let $T$ be a list sorted non-strictly by $f$, that is, $f(j) \le f(k)$ whenever $j$ occurs before $k$ in $T$. results.title: Left endpoint of a segment

results.title: Right endpoint of a segment
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Endpoint of an event
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The point of the sweep event $(i, b)$ is the left endpoint of segment $i$ when $b$ is true (a left-endpoint event) and the right endpoint of segment $i$ when $b$ is false.

results.title: Left endpoint events precede right endpoint events
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered set and $S$ a family of segments in $K^2$, each given by its two endpoints. For every segment $i$ of $S$, the left endpoint event of $i$ is strictly smaller than its right endpoint event in the sweep order on events (by $x$-coordinate, then left endpoints before right endpoints, then by $y$-coordinate).

results.title: A sweep prefix with a right endpoint has its left endpoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered set and $S$ a family of $n$ segments in $K^2$, each given by its two endpoints. If the sorted sweep event list of $S$ is a list $P$ followed by a list $Q$, and $P$ contains the right endpoint event of a segment $j$, then $P$ also contains the left endpoint event of $j$.

results.title: Splitting a list at the first occurrence of a member
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $i$ occurs in a list $T$ of indices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, then $T$ is the longest initial part of $T$ not containing $i$, followed by $i$, followed by the part of $T$ after the first occurrence of $i$.

results.title: The sweep status holds the active segments

results.title: Meeting segments

results.title: Neighbours on the sweep status are disjoint
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be an initial part of the sorted list of events. If running the sweep over $P$ from the empty status list reports no intersection and ends with status list $T$, then no two consecutive segments of $T$ meet.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rate matrix of the two-locus ancestral process of a sample of two, with time in units of `2 N` generations and `ρ = 4 N r`: coalescence at rate `1` for every pair of ancestral lineages, recombination at rate `ρ / 2` for every lineage ancestral at both loci.

results.title: The two-locus coalescent rate matrix is a rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `ρ ≥ 0`, `twoLocusRate ρ` is a rate matrix.

results.title: Common denominator of the two-locus moments
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The common denominator `ρ² + 13 ρ + 18` of the two-locus moments.

results.title: Positivity of the two-locus moment denominator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The denominator `ρ² + 13 ρ + 18` is positive for `ρ ≥ 0`.

results.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `A`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `ρ ≥ 0`, the backward equations of `E_i T_A` (`m i = 0` where `A` has coalesced, `(Q m) i = -1` elsewhere) force `m i = 1` in every state where `A` has not coalesced: locus `A` alone is Kingman's coalescent of two genes.

results.title: Mean coalescence time at locus `B`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Mean coalescence time at locus `B` (the mirror image of `eq_one_of_meanTimeA`).

results.title: Second moment of `T_A`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `m` solves the mean equations of `eq_one_of_meanTimeA` and `g` the second-moment equations (`g i = 0` where `A` has coalesced, `(Q g) i = -2 m i` elsewhere), then `g i = 2` where `A` has not coalesced, so the variance read off from these equations is `2 - 1² = 1`.

results.title: Covariance of coalescence times at two linked loci
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The covariance `Cov(T_A, T_B) = (ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13 ρ + 18)` of the coalescence times at two loci of two sequences sampled linked (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson 1985).

results.title: Two-locus covariance under complete linkage

results.title: Positivity of the two-locus covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The covariance is positive for `ρ ≥ 0`.

results.title: Two-locus covariance is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The covariance is at most `Var T_A = 1` for `ρ ≥ 0` (outside this domain the formula can exceed `1`; e.g. `twoLocusCov (-1) = 17 / 6`).

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Generator of the two-locus Wright–Fisher diffusion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generator of the two-locus Wright–Fisher diffusion on polynomials in the gamete frequencies, time in units of `2 N` generations, `ρ = 4 N r`, symmetric mutation at rate `ν` per locus in each direction (`ν = θ / 2`, `θ = 4 N u`): `L f = ½ ∑ x_g (δ_{gh} - x_h) ∂_g ∂_h f + ∑ (-(ρ/2) ε_g D + ν (x_{g'} + x_{g''} - 2 x_g)) ∂_g f`.

results.title: Drift of gamete frequencies matches recombination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Without mutation the drift of a gamete frequency is `2 N` times its per-generation change under `Linkage.recombine` when `ρ = 4 N r`.

results.title: Hill–Robertson / Ohta–Kimura, first row
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the simplex, `L D² = -(3 + ρ + 8ν) D² + D (1 - 2p)(1 - 2q) + p (1 - p) q (1 - q)` (for all real `ρ`, `ν`).

results.title: Hill–Robertson / Ohta–Kimura, second row
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the simplex, `L (D z) = 4 D² - (5 + ρ/2 + 8ν) D z` with `z = (1 - 2p)(1 - 2q)`.

results.title: Hill–Robertson / Ohta–Kimura, third row
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the simplex, `L Π = D z - (2 + 8ν) Π + ν (p (1 - p) + q (1 - q))`; for `ν = 0` the three rows close.

results.title: Stationary law of the two-locus diffusion
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A stationary law of the two-locus diffusion in the weak (basic adjoint) sense: a probability measure on the gamete-frequency simplex with `∫ L f dμ = 0` for every polynomial `f`.

results.title: Stationary standardized linkage disequilibrium $\sigma_d^2$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stationary standardized disequilibrium `σ_d² = (10 + ρ + 16ν) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ² + 128ν + 24ρν + 128ν²)`.

results.title: Ohta–Kimura `σ_d²`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a stationary law with `ρ, ν ≥ 0` and `E Π > 0`, `E D² / E[p (1 - p) q (1 - q)] = sigmaDSq ρ ν`.

results.title: Ohta–Kimura formula for $\sigma_d^2$ without mutation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The low-mutation value `σ_d² = (10 + ρ) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ²)` (Ohta & Kimura 1971).

results.title: Low-mutation limit of $\sigma_d^2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `σ_d² → (10 + ρ) / (22 + 13ρ + ρ²)` as the mutation rate tends to `0`, for `ρ ≥ 0`.

results.title: Product moment of the two coalescence times, path form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Product moment of the two coalescence times, path form (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson 1985): from two linked sequences, `E (T_A T_B) = 1 + (ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)`.

results.title: Covariance of the coalescence times, path form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Covariance of the coalescence times, path form (Hudson 1983; Kaplan & Hudson 1985): for the two-locus ancestral process started from two linked sequences, `E (T_A T_B) - E T_A E T_B = (ρ + 18) / (ρ² + 13ρ + 18)`, with all three expectations finite lower Lebesgue integrals of the hitting times.
